cause: The robot drove forward along a narrow indoor passage and its right wheel struck and climbed the leg/footrest rung of a wooden barstool on its right at ~8.5 s (video time; ~6.86 s IMU time), causing the robot to violently roll ~90 degrees onto its left side.
evidence: 00:00.000-00:06.000 (video): Robot sits stationary on a flat indoor hardwood floor facing a gap between a staircase railing on the left and kitchen island barstools on the right (a slight camera nudge occurs at 00:03.250 as a cat jumps onto the stool, corresponding to t=1.5 s in the IMU log).
00:06.125 (video) / t=4.28 s (IMU): Robot begins driving straight forward toward the gap at ~0.6-0.7 m/s (showing a ~1.8 s clock offset between video and IMU timestamps).
00:08.125-00:08.500 (video) / t=6.56-6.86 s (IMU): The front-right wheel contacts the wooden barstool leg/rung (~0.15 m to the right of centerline), pitching and rolling the chassis.

00:08.625-00:09.250 (video) / t=6.96-7.56 s (IMU): The robot tips past recovery to its left; IMU records sharp impact spikes (az_g = -1.639 g at t=7.06 s and -1.948 g at t=7.46 s) as it slams onto its left side.

00:09.375-00:11.875 (video) / t=7.76-11.94 s (IMU): Robot rests completely on its left side facing the ceiling, confirmed by IMU steady-state gravity on the lateral axis (ay_g ≈ +1.02 g, az_g ≈ -0.02 g).

other_factors: Wooden barstool with a low horizontal footrest rung between the legs that the right wheel climbed
Approximately 1.75-1.80 s synchronization offset between the video clock and the IMU log (IMU timestamps lead video timestamps)

unknowns: Exact synchronization offset (~1.75-1.80 s) between the video timestamps and IMU log timestamps; both sensors agree on the physical sequence of events (nudge, drive start, collision, and 90-degree left rollover), so both are trusted for dynamics while noting the clock skew.
Exact forward speed and initial distance to the stool leg (estimated from visual floor plank scale and travel time without wheel odometry).
